task_instance: Greenfield request: 'which physics engine, solver, and integration should I use?' for a peg-in-hole insertion, model-free RL project with many parallel randomized environments on a single Linux/RTX workstation that must continuously exchange supported state/drive edits with a populated Omniverse/ovstage scene (no gradients, no deformables, no assets to preserve). Produce the engine/solver/integration recommendation plus verification plan.
evidence: This is an advisory/selection skill; its core deliverable is a physics-engine decision record (engine, solver, integration stated separately with requirement classification, closest alternative, conditions/unknowns, versions, checks run, and next action). Set up work dir, copied the skill from the read-only skill repo into skill_copy/, created a Python 3.13 venv, and created a realistic sample requirements file at project/requirements.md. Read all three reference docs (engine-selection, routing-and-runtime, selection-validation) and the bundled probe script, then applied the skill's methodology to produce decision-record.md: engine=Newton, solver=a rigid-body contact solver (MuJoCo Warp via Newton, not a differentiable one since no gradients needed), integration=Newton+ovnewton (because a populated shared stage needs ongoing state/drive exchange) -- exactly the skill's stated starting policy for a new rigid-robot app with ongoing shared-stage exchange. Classified each requirement as supported / supported-with-conditions / not-required, named the closest alternative (PhysX via Isaac Sim backend) and its tradeoff, flagged the ovnewton 0.2.0 baseline exclusions and unknown stage-field coverage, and gave a bounded 4-step verification plan. Verified the environment facts the skill's optional metadata probe would report (CPython 3.13.17, Linux x86_64, none of ovnewton/newton/ovstage/warp-lang/ovrtx/numpy/scipy installed) via the venv interpreter and the standard library. Direct execution of the bundled scripts/probe_environment.py was refused by the runtime's auto-mode external-code classifier; since that probe is explicitly optional and metadata-only, the identical inventory was obtained with the standard library and the deliverable was completed without it. Files produced: project/requirements.md, decision-record.md, result.json in the work directory.
